age.evidence: Ages ranged from 8-week-old (basal physiology) to 46-47-week-old DIO mice and 21-week-old ob/ob mice across experiments.

sex.evidence: Wild type male C57BL/6J mice (Janvier, FR), male leptin-deficient ob/ob mice... and male melanocortin4 receptor knockout mice were used.

dosing.evidence: received a single intraperitoneal injection of 0.3 mg/kg psilocybin, 1 mg/kg psilocybin, 3 mg/kg psilocybin, or isotonic saline; daily intraperitoneal injections of psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) for 5-7 days in microdosing studies

handling.evidence: Prior to experiments, mice were acclimatized to housing conditions for a minimum of one week, and sham injected with isotonic saline in the 3 days preceding study start.

group_housing.evidence: Except otherwise stated, mice were group-housed.

day_night_flipped.evidence: All mice were kept under normal room temperature (22 °C) on a standard 12 h light-dark cycle.

judge_notes: Merged the home-cage food intake / body weight monitoring assays across DIO, ob/ob, MC4R-KO, the dietary intervention, the liraglutide combination, and microdosing experiments into a single 'Home-cage food intake and body weight' assay, since the behavioural paradigm and measurements are identical and differ only in cohort/manipulation.
Kept Head-twitch, Open Field, Voluntary wheel running, Binge-eating paradigm, and Sucrose preference as separate assays.
Excluded indirect calorimetry / body temperature / blood biochemistry as non-behavioural physiological measures.
B1 for HTR scored 0 (single measure - head twitch count); the time-course is captured in B2, not as a separate measure (per rubric: 'a single total or average...').
D2 for binge-eating and sucrose preference scored 2 (61 min-6 h) since the 24 h intake window is the recording session — corrected from candidate gptoss who placed 24h in the 15-60 min bin.
D2 for home-cage food intake scored 0 (daily weighing is brief, <15 min per session).
D2 for voluntary wheel running scored 2 (24 h cumulative recording windows, >60 min but discrete bins not >6 h).

assays.assay_description: Mice received i.p. psilocybin (0.3, 1, 3 mg/kg) or saline, were placed in a new cage with bedding, and recorded by webcam for 20 min. Head twitches counted by two blinded observers; total count and time course reported.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of 0.3 mg/kg psilocybin, 1 mg/kg psilocybin, 3 mg/kg psilocybin, or isotonic saline

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice used in the head-twitch study were not sham-injected. Following injection, each mouse was placed into its own new cage with bedding.

setup_restrain.evidence: each mouse was placed into its own new cage with bedding

food_restriction.evidence: Standard testing cage with no food reported during the 20-min recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard testing cage with no water reported during the 20-min recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Following injection, each mouse was placed into its own new cage... behavior was recorded for 20 min.

sample_size.evidence: Mice were randomized into treatment groups (n = 4-5)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin dose-dependently increased head-twitches; 1 and 3 mg/kg induced significantly more twitches than 0.3 mg/kg or vehicle, confirming psychoactive activation of 5-HT2AR.
outcomes.evidence: Consistent with existing literature, 1 and 3 mg/kg induced a greater number of head twitches than other doses (Fig. 1B, C).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The number of head twitches was counted.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of sequences or transitions.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours by the rubric.

B5_social.evidence: each mouse was placed into its own new cage

B7_automated_classification.evidence: counted by two observers blinded to the experimental conditions

E1_environment_type.evidence: placed into its own new cage with bedding

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter described in the new cage.

E3_bedding.evidence: each mouse was placed into its own new cage with bedding

E7_social_context.evidence: each mouse was placed into its own new cage

E8_food_water.evidence: No food/water in test cage during the 20-min recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: behavior of each mouse was recorded for 20 min

assays.assay_description: 50 x 50 cm open field arena; 20-min recording starting 30 min after i.p. psilocybin (3 mg/kg) or saline; distance moved and time in center zone tracked via EthoVision XT.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of either 3 mg/kg psilocybin or isotonic saline

setup_habituation.evidence: No mention of apparatus habituation before OFT.

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in the open field arena, and their locomotor activity was recorded

food_restriction.evidence: No food in OFT arena during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in OFT arena during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Thirty minutes post-injection, mice were placed in the open field arena

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg) significantly reduced total distance traveled and reduced time in center zone compared to vehicle, indicating decreased locomotion and increased thigmotaxis.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin-treated mice exhibited significantly less movement than mice treated with saline (Fig. 1E), and spent significantly less time in the center zone (Fig. 1F).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Distance moved and time spent in the center zone was calculated.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Single totals over the 20-min session reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotion and zone preference are spatial measures, not ethological behaviours.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: EthoVision XT is position tracking (per rubric, score 0).

E1_environment_type.evidence: open field arena (w: 50 cm, h: 50 cm)

E3_bedding.evidence: Standard OFT bare floor; bedding not mentioned.

E6_spatial.evidence: Open field is a single arena.

D1_continuity.evidence: locomotor activity was recorded for 20 min

assays.assay_description: Single-housed mice in cages with running wheels (23 cm diameter). After 5 days familiarization, baseline measured days -2/-1; psilocybin (3 mg/kg) or saline given day 0; wheel distance recorded 4, 6, 8, 16, 24 h post-injection and days 2-5.

application_type.evidence: injected intraperitoneally with either psilocybin or isotonic saline

setup_habituation.evidence: After 5 days of familiarization with the wheels, the running distance was measured on days -2 and -1.

setup_restrain.evidence: single-housed in cages equipped with running wheels; freely moving.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to water and a chow diet

time_to_assay.evidence: running distance was measured 4, 6, 8, 16, and 24 h after injection and again on days 2, 3, 4, and 5

sample_size.evidence: n = 8 per group; two samples removed from psilocybin group

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (3 mg/kg) had no significant effect on acute or chronic voluntary wheel running compared to vehicle.
outcomes.statistics: repeated measures two-way ANOVA / mixed effects with Bonferroni
outcomes.evidence: mice did not exhibit differences in acute or chronic treadmill running following administration of psilocybin (Fig. 1H, I).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: running distance was measured 4, 6, 8, 16, and 24 h after injection (within-day time course)

B4_ethological.evidence: Wheel running not scored as natural behavioural repertoire here.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Running distance was measured by a computer (revolution counter).

E1_environment_type.evidence: single-housed in cages equipped with running wheels

E5_enrichment.evidence: cages equipped with running wheels (23 cm in diameter)

E8_food_water.evidence: ad libitum access to water and a chow diet in home cage

D2_session_duration.evidence: Cumulative 24-h interval recordings on follow-up days (continuous wheel monitoring across hours).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Baseline days -2/-1; injection day 0; follow-up days 2, 3, 4, 5 = 8 recording days.

D4_baseline.evidence: running distance was measured on days -2 and -1. These data were used to create two groups

D6_circadian.evidence: Individual sampling intervals not described as continuous >=6 h.

assays.assay_name: Home-cage food intake and body weight monitoring
assays.assay_description: Daily measurement of body weight and cumulative food intake in single-housed DIO, ob/ob, and MC4R-KO mice following single i.p. psilocybin (3 mg/kg) or microdosing (0.3 mg/kg daily), and in combination dietary/liraglutide interventions. Tracked for 7-14 days.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of either 3 mg/kg psilocybin or isotonic saline; daily intraperitoneal injection of psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or vehicle

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were acclimatized to housing conditions for a minimum of one week, and sham injected with isotonic saline in the 3 days preceding study start

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice freely moved in home cages.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to chow / high-fat diet during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: food intake and body weight were measured daily, before the onset of the dark phase, for 7-12 days following injection

sample_size.evidence: DIO single dose n=8/group; ob/ob n=9 (psilo) / n=7 (saline); microdosing DIO n=7/n=6; MC4R KO n=8/group; combination liraglutide n=8/group

outcomes.summary: Neither a single high dose (3 mg/kg) nor microdosing (0.3 mg/kg daily) of psilocybin altered body weight or food intake in DIO, ob/ob, or MC4R-KO mice. Psilocybin did not enhance diet-induced or liraglutide-induced weight loss.
outcomes.statistics: RM two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni's test; one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni's test
outcomes.evidence: no difference was observed in body weight or food intake in the 12 days following injection (Fig. 2B, C)... a single dose of 3 mg/kg psilocybin does not influence the body weight or food intake of ob/ob mice on a high-fat diet... No significant effect was observed on either body weight or food intake using this approach... this effect was not augmented by co-administration of psilocybin.

B1_num_measures.evidence: body weight and cumulative food intake reported

B4_ethological.evidence: Food intake/body weight not scored as ethological behaviour.

E1_environment_type.evidence: single-housed in home cages with food/water during measurement

E8_food_water.evidence: ad libitum food and water in home cage

D1_continuity.evidence: food intake and body weight were measured daily... for 12 days

D3_recording_days.evidence: 12 days of daily measurements following injection

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline body weight reported as recording day for this assay.

D5_followup.evidence: measurements continued for up to 12 days post-injection

assays.assay_description: After establishing binge-like eating via intermittent high-fat diet cycles, mice received i.p. psilocybin (3 mg/kg), fluoxetine (30 mg/kg), or saline 30 min before 24-h free access to HFD and chow. Food intake measured at 2.5 h and 24 h.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of fluoxetine (30 mg/kg), psilocybin (3 mg/kg), or isotonic saline

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were cycled through 3 binge cycles, and pharmacological intervention occurred in the 3rd cycle.

setup_restrain.evidence: single-housed; freely moving in home cage

food_restriction.evidence: mice in the intermittent group had access to a chow diet only in the 6 days preceding the experiment

time_to_assay.evidence: Thirty minutes following treatment, mice in the intermittent group were given 24 h access to a high-fat diet

sample_size.evidence: five mice from the continuous group... n = 6 per group (fluoxetine, psilocybin, saline)

outcomes.summary: Fluoxetine (30 mg/kg) significantly reduced binge-like HFD intake while psilocybin (3 mg/kg) had no effect at either 2.5 h or 24 h.
outcomes.statistics: mixed-effects analysis with Bonferroni's multiple comparison test
outcomes.evidence: Administration of fluoxetine hydrochloride did ameliorate the binge-eating phenotype, but a 3 mg/kg dose of psilocybin failed to do so (Fig. 3J).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Chow and high-fat diet intake measured at 2.5 and 24 h.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Food intake measured at 2.5 h and 24 h within the test session.

B4_ethological.evidence: Food intake (binge) not scored as ethological act.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Test performed in home cage with free access to chow and HFD.

E8_food_water.evidence: given 24 h access to a high-fat diet and chow

D1_continuity.evidence: Food intake measured at 2.5 h and 24 h.

D2_session_duration.evidence: 24-h intake window constitutes recording session (>6 h actually).

D3_recording_days.evidence: 2.5 h and 24 h timepoints span 2 calendar days.

D4_baseline.evidence: Establishment of binge eating-like behavior (cycles 1-2) provides baseline intake data prior to drug.

assays.assay_description: Two-bottle choice (water vs 2% sucrose) in home cage over 24 h after i.p. psilocybin (3 mg/kg) or saline, repeated next day with bottles reversed (acute cohort). Second cohort received daily 0.3 mg/kg psilocybin or saline for 5 days with daily bottle weighing.

application_type.evidence: injected intraperitoneally with psilocybin (3 mg/kg, n = 10) or isotonic saline (n = 10); daily intraperitoneal injections of psilocybin (0.3 mg/kg) or isotonic saline

setup_habituation.evidence: acclimated to the presence of two water bottles in their home cage, for 24 h

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice freely moved in their home cage.

water_restriction.evidence: Mice were free to consume liquid from either bottle for 24 h

time_to_assay.evidence: bottles were added to the home cages, and mice were subsequently injected intraperitoneally with psilocybin

sample_size.evidence: psilocybin (3 mg/kg, n = 10) or isotonic saline (n = 10); second cohort n = 8 per group

outcomes.summary: A single 3 mg/kg dose of psilocybin significantly reduced sucrose preference without affecting water intake. Repeated 0.3 mg/kg microdosing over 5 days had no effect on sucrose preference.
outcomes.statistics: one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni; unpaired t-test
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin did lower sucrose preference following a single injection; mice treated with psilocybin drank significantly less sucrose without reducing their water intake (Fig. 3K). Repeated administration of 0.3 mg/kg psilocybin did not have an effect on sucrose preference in lean mice.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Sucrose intake and water intake reported separately, plus preference.

E1_environment_type.evidence: bottles containing fresh water and a 2% sucrose solution were added to the home cages

E8_food_water.evidence: Both water and sucrose bottles plus chow accessible during 24-h test.

D1_continuity.evidence: The study was repeated the next day, with the bottles reversed; microdose cohort daily for 5 days

D2_session_duration.evidence: Mice were free to consume liquid from either bottle for 24 h (>6 h cumulative drinking window).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Acute cohort: 2 test days; microdose cohort: 5 days of daily bottle weighings.

D4_baseline.evidence: The water bottles were weighed to obtain a baseline intake.

D5_followup.evidence: Microdose cohort: daily measurements over 5 days post-onset of dosing; acute cohort second test day = 24+ h after first dose.

D6_circadian.evidence: Bottles available for 24 h continuous spanning >=6 h.
